statements.claim: The herd went ahead of the people, with horns sounding as the cowherds travelled
statements.evidence: 10.11.31: godhānāni puraskṛtya śṛṅgāṇy āpūrya sarvataḥ (cattle placed before, horns blown on all sides)

statements.claim: The women rode in the carts, freshly adorned for the road
statements.evidence: 10.11.32: gopyo rūḍha-rathā nūtna-kuca-kuṅkuma-kāntayaḥ

statements.claim: Yasoda and Rohini sat side by side in one cart
statements.evidence: 10.11.33: yaśodā-rohiṇyāv ekaṃ śakaṭam āsthite

statements.claim: They were bound for Vrindavan, a forest that stays pleasant in every season
statements.evidence: 10.11.34: vṛndāvanaṃ sampraviśya sarva-kāla-sukhāvaham

statements.claim: The hill of Govardhana rose to one side and the Yamuna ran past with sandy banks
statements.evidence: 10.11.35: vṛndāvanaṃ govardhanaṃ yamunā-pulināni ca

statements.claim: They pitched their camp in a crescent of wagons
statements.evidence: Pack summary confirms they 'pitch their camp'; the crescent-of-wagons arrangement is descriptive detail not asserted by the verses

statements.claim: Krishna and Balarama were somewhere among the boys in the procession
statements.evidence: Generic placement detail; not asserted in 10.11.31-35

notes: All sourceable claims match 10.11.31-35. No UNSUPPORTED/CONTRADICTED.

statements.claim: After the cowherds settled, the boys took up tending the calves
statements.evidence: 10.11.36-37 (delighting Vraja folk with the cowherd boys) and 40 (tending calves on the Yamuna bank)

statements.claim: The boys played the flute, cast throwing-ropes, and wrestled bellowing like young bulls
statements.evidence: 10.11.38-39: veṇuṃ vādayanto; kṣepaṇaiḥ kṣipataḥ; vṛṣāyamāṇau nardantau yuyudhāte parasparam

statements.claim: The demon Vatsasura took the shape of a calf and mingled with the herd
statements.evidence: 10.11.41: taṃ vatsa-rūpiṇaṃ ... vatsa-yūtha-gataṃ hariḥ

statements.claim: Krishna seized it by the hind legs together with the tail
statements.evidence: 10.11.42: gṛhītvāpara-pādābhyāṃ saha-lāṅgūlam acyutaḥ

statements.claim: He whirled the creature and dashed it lifeless against a wood-apple (kapittha) tree
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt ('whirls him by his hind legs and dashes him lifeless against a tree') and index summary ('hurls him dead into a kapittha tree')

statements.claim: The astonished boys shouted 'Well done! Well done!'
statements.evidence: 10.11.43: taṃ vīkṣya vismitā bālāḥ śaśaṃsuḥ sādhu sādhv iti

statements.claim: The two who tended calves were the keepers of all the worlds
statements.evidence: 10.11.44: tau vatsa-pālakau bhūtvā sarva-lokaika-pālakau

statements.claim: The boys found a huge crane standing on the pasture
statements.evidence: 10.11.46: te tatra dadṛśur bālā mahā-sattvam avasthitam

statements.claim: It was the demon Baka in crane form, a friend of Kamsa
statements.evidence: 10.11.47: bako nāma mahān asuro baka-rūpa-dhṛk; 10.11.50: kaṃsa-sakham

statements.claim: The crane swallowed Krishna whole in a single motion
statements.evidence: 10.11.48: kṛṣṇaṃ mahā-baka-grastaṃ dṛṣṭvā

statements.claim: Inside, Krishna burned the root of the crane's palate like fire, and the crane could not bear him and flung him out
statements.evidence: 10.11.49: taṃ tālu-mūlaṃ pradahantam agnivad; 10.11.50: tam āpatantaṃ (the demon then attacks again, implying it had expelled him)

statements.claim: Krishna seized the two halves of the bird's beak and tore it apart
statements.evidence: 10.11.50: sa nigṛhya tuṇḍayor dorbhyāṃ bakaṃ ... satāṃ patiḥ

statements.claim: The boys' breath seemed to return to them, like the senses when life returns
statements.evidence: 10.11.52: muktaṃ bakāsyād upalabhya bālakā rāmādayaḥ prāṇam ivendriyo gaṇaḥ

statements.claim: The heaven-dwellers rained a shower of flowers
statements.evidence: 10.11.51: sura-loka-vāsinaḥ samākiran nandana-mallikādibhiḥ

statements.claim: Aghasura was the younger brother of Putana and Bakasura
statements.evidence: 10.12.13: bakī-bakānujaḥ (younger brother of Bakī/Putana and Baka)

statements.claim: Kamsa had instructed him, and he sought revenge for his slain kin
statements.evidence: 10.12.13: kaṃsānuśiṣṭaḥ ... ayaṃ tu me sodara-nāśa-kṛt

statements.claim: He stretched his body into a python a yojana long and thick as a great mountain
statements.evidence: 10.12.15: yojanāyāma-mahādri-pīvaram

statements.claim: His lower lip rested on the earth, his upper lip touched the clouds, and his teeth rose like mountain peaks
statements.evidence: 10.12.16: dharādharoṣṭho jaladottaroṣṭho dary-ānanānto giri-śṛṅga-daṃṣṭraḥ

statements.claim: The boys mistook the demon for a marvel of the forest — a mountain lying down, a cave, a cloud with a sun-reddened edge
statements.evidence: 10.12.17-22 (matvā vṛndāvana-śriyam; sattva-kūṭam; arka-karāraktam; uttarā-hanuvad ghanam; nagodare)

statements.claim: The boys joked that if it swallowed them it would die as Baka had died
statements.evidence: 10.12.23: asmān kim atra grasitā niviṣṭān ayaṃ tathā ced bakavad vinaṅkṣyati

statements.claim: Only Krishna recognized the demon and resolved that its mouth would not close on his friends
statements.evidence: 10.12.24: rakṣo viditvākhila-bhūta-hṛt-sthitaḥ ... svānāṃ niroddhuṃ bhagavān mano dadhe

statements.claim: Brahma had watched Krishna walk into the python-demon's mouth and lead his friends out alive, and was filled with wonder
statements.evidence: 10.13.14: dṛṣṭvāghāsura-mokṣaṇaṃ prabhavataḥ prāptaḥ paraṃ vismayam

statements.claim: He had seen a great light leave the dead demon and enter the boy
statements.evidence: Detail is from the preceding canonical event (evt_0059 / DKS_0047, 10.12.32: jyotiḥ ... pīnāhi-bhogotthitam, 'a great radiance from the demon's body enters Krishna' per that pack's summary), which 10.13.14 references; not in the 10.13.11-16 passages themselves

statements.claim: While the boys ate on a sandbank, the calves strayed and Krishna went alone to bring them back
statements.evidence: 10.13.11 (bhuñjāneṣu), 10.13.13 (adri-darī-kuñja-gahvareṣv ātma-vatsakān), 10.13.15 (puline)

statements.claim: Brahma secretly carried off both the boys and the calves and hid them away by his power
statements.evidence: 10.13.14: nītvānyatra ... antaradadhāt khe 'vasthitaḥ

statements.claim: Krishna returned to find no boys and no calves, and searched the deep forest without finding them
statements.evidence: 10.13.15-16: vatsān adṛṣṭvaitya puline 'pi ca vatsapān / kvāpy adṛṣṭvāntar-vipine vatsān pālāṃś ca viśva-vit

statements.claim: The sandbank lay quiet behind him, and none of the boys thought to be afraid
statements.evidence: 10.13.12: tān dṛṣṭvā bhaya-santrastān ūce kṛṣṇo 'sya bhī-bhayam — the pack says Krishna saw the boys fear-stricken and spoke to dispel their fear; the story asserts the boys were not afraid

statements.claim: He knew at once what had happened and who had done it, for nothing is hidden from him
statements.evidence: 10.13.16: viśva-vit (the all-knowing)

corrections.original_sentence: The sandbank lay quiet behind him, and none of the boys thought to be afraid.
corrections.suggested: The sandbank lay quiet behind him, and the boys, whose sudden fear Krishna had just quieted with a word, were at ease.

notes: One CONTRADICTED: 10.13.12 has the boys fear-stricken (bhaya-santrastān) with Krishna dispelling their fear; the story instead says they were not afraid. The 'great light entering the boy' is supported via the preceding event pack (DKS_0047 / 10.12.32).

statements.claim: To Brahma only a moment had passed; in Vrindavan a year
statements.evidence: 10.13.39 (ātmamānena truṭy-anehasā, in the twinkling of an eye) and 10.14.42 (ekasminn api yāte 'bde, though a year had passed)

statements.claim: Brahma found the calves and boys exactly as before; the cows hurried from afar to their calves and the elders embraced the children with a love deeper than before
statements.evidence: 10.13.28-33 (gāvo vatsān upavrajam ... apāyayan; jātānurāgā gata-manyavo 'rbhakān; tokāśleṣa-sunirvṛtāḥ)

statements.claim: Brahma could not tell what he had hidden from what he now saw
statements.evidence: 10.13.41: ita ete 'tra kutratyā man-māyā-mohitetare

statements.claim: His attempt to use illusion failed — like a firefly's glow at noon or darkness/mist at dawn
statements.evidence: 10.13.43-44: sammohayan viṣṇuṃ vimohaṃ ... khadyotārcir ivāhani

statements.claim: All the cowherd boys appeared as four-armed forms holding conch, discus, mace and lotus, marked with shrivatsa, armlets and bracelets, garlanded in fresh tulsi, smiling like moonlight with sidelong glances
statements.evidence: 10.13.45-49 (catur-bhujāḥ śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-rājīva-pāṇayaḥ; śrīvatsāṅgada-do-ratna-kambu-kaṅkaṇa-pāṇayaḥ; tulasī-nava-dāmabhiḥ; candrikā-viśada-smeraiḥ sāruṇāpāṅga-vīkṣitaiḥ)

statements.claim: Around them stood all the worlds and powers, from the first gods down to the last blade of grass, each in its own form
statements.evidence: 10.13.50-53 (ātmādi-stamba-paryantair mūrtimadbhiś carācaraiḥ; satya-jñānānantānanda-mātraika-rasa-mūrtayaḥ)

statements.claim: The eleven senses of Brahma froze, and Krishna drew the curtain of maya over his sight; he rose as one waking from the dead
statements.evidence: 10.13.55-57 (stimitaikādaśendriyaḥ; cacchādājo jñātvā ... javanikām; kaḥ paretavad utthitaḥ)

statements.claim: He saw the ordinary world with men and animals sitting together without natural enmity, and a small boy with a morsel of food searching for his friends as before
statements.evidence: 10.13.58-60 (naisarga-durvairāḥ sahāsan nṛ-mṛgādayaḥ; ekaṃ sa-pāṇi-kavalaṃ ... vicinvad)

statements.claim: Brahma descended from his swan, cast himself down like a golden rod, touched Krishna's feet with the tips of his four crowns and bathed them with tears
statements.evidence: 10.13.61 (nija-dhoraṇato 'vatīrya; pṛthvyāṃ vapuḥ kanaka-daṇḍam ivābhipātya; spṛṣṭvā catur-mukuṭa-koṭibhir aṅghri-yugmaṃ; mud-aśru-sujalair akṛtābhiṣekam)

statements.claim: Krishna's body is made of his own will, not of matter
statements.evidence: 10.14.1: svecchā-mayasya na tu bhūta-mayasya

statements.claim: Those who abandon the effort to know and simply bow and listen live by the truth; those who strive only for knowledge labour like threshers of empty husks
statements.evidence: 10.14.2-3 (jñāne prayāsam udapāsya namanta eva ...; kliśyanti ye kevala-bodha-labdhaye ... sthūla-tuṣāvaghātinām)

statements.claim: Even the purest-hearted and great seers cannot measure his greatness
statements.evidence: 10.14.5-6 (mahimāguṇasya te viboddhum arhaty amalāntar-ātmabhiḥ; guṇān vimātuṃ ... ka īśire)

statements.claim: 'I was born of passion and in my ignorance thought myself a lord apart from you; forgive me'
statements.evidence: 10.14.8-9 (rajo-bhuvo hy ajānatas tvat-pṛthag-īśa-māninaḥ; ataḥ kṣamasvācyuta)

statements.claim: 'Where am I, a body of seven hand-spans in this egg of the universe, and where is your greatness, in the pores of whose skin whole worlds course?'
statements.evidence: 10.14.10 (kvāhaṃ ... sapta-vitasti-kāyaḥ; kvedṛg-vidhāvigaṇitāṇḍa-parāṇu-caryā-vātādhva-roma-vivarasya ca te mahitvam)

statements.claim: 'First you were one, then all the cowherd boys and calves, then an endless company of four-armed forms, then as many universes — and what remained was the one, the unlimited'
statements.evidence: 10.14.17 (eko 'si prathamaṃ tato vraja-suhṛd-vatsāḥ samastā api; tāvanto 'si catur-bhujās ...; tāvanty eva jaganty abhūs tad amitaṃ brahmādvayaṃ śiṣyate)

statements.claim: 'This whole world is as unreal as a dream and full of sorrow, yet through your maya it shines as if real, resting on you alone'
statements.evidence: 10.14.21 (svapnābham asta-dhiṣaṇaṃ puru-duḥkha-duḥkham; tvayy eva ... māyāta udyad api yat sad ivāvabhāti)

statements.claim: 'You are Narayana, the Self of every being and the witness of every world; from your navel all this rose again when the worlds had dissolved into water'
statements.evidence: 10.14.12-13 (jagat-trayāntodadhi-samplavode nārāyaṇasyodara-nābhi-nālāt; nārāyaṇas tvaṃ ... ātmāsy adhīśākhila-loka-sākṣī)

statements.claim: The women of Vraja who fed him at the breast drank nectar; the dust of his feet is sought by the Vedas
statements.evidence: 10.14.30-33 (stanyāmṛtaṃ pītam atīva te mudā; yat-pada-rajaḥ śruti-mṛgyam eva)

statements.claim: 'Give me leave, Krishna; you know everything there is to know'
statements.evidence: 10.14.38: anujānīhi māṃ kṛṣṇa sarvaṃ tvaṃ vetsi sarva-dṛk

statements.claim: Brahma circumambulated Krishna three times, bowed, and departed for his own realm
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt summary ('walking three times around him and bowing, departs for his own realm') and 10.14.41 (tato 'nujñāpya bhagavān sva-bhuvaṃ prāg avasthitān)

statements.claim: After giving Brahma leave, Krishna returned the boys and calves to the sandbank as though nothing had happened
statements.evidence: 10.14.41-42 and pack excerpt summary ('Krishna brings the boys and calves back to the sandbank as though nothing had happened')

statements.claim: A full year had passed, but the boys, their minds covered by maya, remembered nothing of it
statements.evidence: 10.14.42-43 (ekasminn api yāte 'bde; kiṃ kiṃ na vismarantīha māyā-mohita-cetasaḥ)

statements.claim: The boys welcomed Krishna with 'Welcome back! You returned quickly!'
statements.evidence: 10.14.44: ūcuś ca suhṛdaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ sv-āgataṃ te 'ti-raṃhasā

statements.claim: Krishna smiled and sat down and ate with the boys, finishing the meal they had left
statements.evidence: 10.14.45: tato hasan hṛṣīkeśo 'bhyavahṛtya sahārbhakaiḥ

statements.claim: Krishna entered the cow-pen decked in peacock feathers, flowers and forest earth-colours, his flute sounding, the boys singing his praises, the gopis' eyes gladdened
statements.evidence: 10.14.46 (barha-prasūna-vana-dhātu-vicitritāṅgaḥ; proddāma-veṇu-dala-śṛṅga-ravotsavāḍhyaḥ; anuga-gīta-pavitra-kīrtir; gopī-dṛg-utsava-dṛśiḥ)

statements.claim: The boys told how the son of Yashoda and Nanda had slain a great serpent that very day, carrying its dried skin as proof
statements.evidence: 10.14.47 (adyānena mahā-vyālo yaśodā-nanda-sūnunā), pack excerpt summary ('carrying the python's dried skin as a trophy'), and 10.12.35 (the dried python skin in Vrindavan)
